gap: 4. CPU vs GPU divergence on the planar three-body problem
whats_missing: Paired CPU and GPU runs of the same planar three-body starts at the same nominal precision, with first-divergence time and outcome statistics, FMA contraction stated.
closest_source_and_why_it_falls_short: Tomihisa 2011 (papers-144): GTX 285 vs Core2 Quad, 3D N=256-4096, RK4; reports only that results 'did not agree', blames FMA truncation, and that __fadd_rn/__dadd_rn remove it at 3-4x cost: no size or time of divergence. Charlie-Zhao N-Body-Simulation (papers-94): CPU and GPU backend agreement at f64 only, with timings, random starts not saved. mikha08-rgb/Nbody (papers-125): GPU f32 against CPU f64 on the figure-eight, so precision and device are not separated.
what_principia_could_produce_and_publish: CPU f64, CPU f32 and GPU f32 (tier a path) on the BZ-1C starts and the Burrau/figure-eight anchors: divergence-time curves and outcome-distribution comparisons, with contraction on/off recorded. Publish the curves and per-run tables.

gap: 5. Per-point fate reproducibility floor at f64
whats_missing: How often a per-start outcome is reproducible under ulp-level perturbation at f64 alone, as a function of event time: the baseline any f32-vs-f64 per-point comparison must beat.
closest_source_and_why_it_falls_short: Ours, from eucliss fatemap.json: mirror pairs (exactly symmetric physics). Over the 42,413 pairs where both members escape, binned by the earlier of the two escape times, the mirrored escaper agrees 0.97 for t < 10 (15,316 pairs), 0.84 for 10-20 (7,778), 0.63 for 20-50 (12,704) and 0.51 past 50 (6,615), chance about 1/3 (the owner's figures of 3 Nov, recounted 3 Nov 2026: 0.974, 0.842, 0.626, 0.512). The triage's earlier count, per pixel, by that pixel's own escape time and a non-escaping mirror counted as disagreeing, they are 0.991 (t 2-6), 0.904 (6-19), 0.610 (21-62), 0.395 (67-200); same for exactly and inexactly mirrored starts, so solver round-off drives it. One unreviewed AI-authored source, f64 only. CFT ens8: one start, 8 members.
what_principia_could_produce_and_publish: The same curve from Principia's own integrator (mirror pairs and summation-order shuffles over the free-fall plane), at f64 and f32, published beside gap 1 so per-point disagreement is read against the floor and only statistics are compared.
